What We Do

Sourcing support from brief to order.

Supplier Research
& Shortlisting

Identify manufacturers that match the product, production capability, order size and destination. Confirm who would make the goods.

Evaluation
& Due Diligence

Review available business records, relevant certificates and evidence of production capability. Flag gaps that need further verification.

Quotation
Comparison

Compare like-for-like quotes on unit price, tooling, minimum order quantities, lead times and trade terms.

Negotiation
& Commercial Terms

Help negotiate pricing, payment milestones and production timelines. Record the specification and terms agreed with the supplier.

Samples
& Quality Checks

Arrange supplier samples and coordinate independent third-party inspections where available against the agreed checklist.

Order Coordination
& Follow-up

Follow up on production milestones within the agreed scope. Help clarify who handles freight and customs under the agreed trade terms.

FAQ

Common questions.

How do you charge for sourcing?

Fees depend on the scope, such as a shortlist, a full quotation comparison or ongoing order support. We agree the scope and fees before work begins and flag supplier or third-party costs for your approval.

Which countries do you source from?

We consider international supply markets based on manufacturing capability, quantity, destination and applicable requirements. Once we have your brief, we discuss which markets make sense.

Can you support samples and quality checks?

We help arrange supplier samples and, where available, coordinate inspections carried out by independent third-party providers. You decide whether the evidence meets your requirements.

More questions
Can you help with small or custom orders?

That depends on tooling, materials and supplier minimums. We can ask about samples or pilot runs and compare how order size affects cost and lead time.

Who handles supplier payments, freight and customs?

Supplier payments follow the terms you approve with the manufacturer. The designated parties handle freight and customs under the agreed trade terms. We can help clarify responsibilities.

What do I need to get started?

A product description, target quantity and delivery country are a good start. Send a drawing, photo, material specification or applicable standard if you have one.
